questions.title: Keyword To Import A Module
questions.description: Which keyword brings a module's code into your script so its names become usable?

questions.title: From Import Grants What
questions.description: What does the statement `from math import sqrt` do?
questions.Option1: It imports the whole math module, so sqrt must be called as math.sqrt(...)
questions.Option2: It binds the name sqrt directly in the current namespace, callable without the module prefix
questions.Option3: It imports every function of every standard-library module at once
questions.Option4: It creates an alias named math for the sqrt function

questions.title: Main Guard Condition
questions.description: When a Python file is executed directly (for example `python app.py`), what is the value of __name__ inside that file?

questions.title: What Is A Python Module
questions.description: In Python, what exactly is a module?
questions.Option1: Any folder that contains code files
questions.Option2: A file with the .py extension containing definitions and statements

questions.title: File That Marks A Package
questions.description: Which file turns an ordinary directory into an importable Python package?

questions.title: Import Alias Keyword
questions.description: Which keyword assigns a shorter alias while importing, as in `import statistics as st`?

questions.title: Accessing Pi After Import
questions.description: After executing `import math`, which expression gives the value of pi?

questions.title: Why Write A Main Guard
questions.description: Why do Python scripts wrap their entry-point code in `if __name__ == "__main__":`?
questions.Option1: It makes the guarded code run noticeably faster
questions.Option2: It ensures that code runs only when the file is executed directly, not when the file is imported as a module
questions.Option3: It is required syntax around every function definition
questions.Option4: It converts the file into an installable package

questions.title: sys.path Holds What
questions.description: What does the list sys.path contain?
questions.Option1: The names of all programs installed on the machine
questions.Option2: The directory locations that are searched, in order, when importing modules
questions.Option3: The contents of the currently executing module
questions.Option4: The URLs pip uses to download packages

questions.title: Tool That Installs Packages
questions.description: Which command-line tool installs third-party packages into site-packages?

questions.title: Payroll Import Simulation Output
questions.description: The file payroll.py shown below is executed directly with `python payroll.py`. What does it print?

questions.title: Floor And Ceil Combo Output
questions.description: What does this script print?
questions.codesnippet:
from math import floor, ceil
print(floor(3.7), ceil(-2.1))

questions.title: Aliased Factorial Sum Output
questions.description: What does this script print?
questions.codesnippet:
from math import factorial as fact
print(fact(3) + fact(4))

questions.title: Circular Import Consequence
questions.description: Two modules, app.py and stats.py, each contain `import <the other one>` at the top of the file. What is the typical consequence when app.py is run?
questions.Option1: Python silently skips the second import and continues
questions.Option2: An ImportError or AttributeError can occur because one module is still partially initialized during the cycle
questions.Option3: Both modules execute twice from start to finish
questions.Option4: Nothing can fail, because imports are always cached and complete

questions.title: Name Variable When Imported
questions.description: A module named utils.py is imported by another script. Inside utils.py, what is the value of __name__ during that import?

questions.title: Seeded Random Pair Sum Output
questions.description: What does this script print? (random.seed(3) makes the sequence fully deterministic.)
questions.codesnippet:
import random
random.seed(3)
a = random.randint(1, 10)
b = random.randint(1, 10)
print(a + b)

questions.title: Two File Import Output
questions.description: utils.py and app.py sit in the same folder. What appears on screen when app.py runs?
questions.Option4: Nothing, because utils.py only defines a library
questions.codesnippet:
# file: utils.py
PI = 3.14

def area(r):
    return PI * r ** 2

print("utils loaded")

# file: app.py
import utils
print(utils.area(2))

questions.title: Search Path Append Check
questions.description: What does this script print?
questions.codesnippet:
import sys

print("app start")
sys.path.append("/opt/plugins")
print("/opt/plugins" in sys.path)

questions.title: Name Print In Two Files
questions.description: tools.py and app.py sit in the same folder. What is printed when `python app.py` runs?
questions.codesnippet:
# file: tools.py
print(__name__)

# file: app.py
import tools
print(__name__)

questions.title: Local Math Shadow Hazard
questions.description: A beginner saves their own helper file as math.py in the project folder and writes `import math` in a script inside that same folder. What most likely happens?
questions.Option1: The standard-library math module wins because built-ins always take priority
questions.Option2: The script's directory is searched first on sys.path, so the local math.py shadows the standard-library module
questions.Option3: Python refuses to run and reports a syntax error about the duplicate name
questions.Option4: Both files are imported and their names are merged into one namespace
